text:
ConocoPhillips rose 3.4% today as oil prices climbed on escalating geopolitical tensions—Ukraine hit Russian oil infrastructure with drone strikes, Iran threatened new responses to U.S. military action, and tanker attacks in the Middle East continued. Brent crude hovered near $110 a barrel, and the gap between the global oil price ($126.55) and U.S. oil price ($101.91) widened, reflecting supply disruptions and shipping constraints that directly boost refiner and producer margins.

The two-week 15.6% rally reflects a broader shift: physical oil delivery costs have surged as tanker rates spike, making the "real" price of crude substantially higher than headline numbers suggest. For an integrated energy company like ConocoPhillips, tighter supply and elevated shipping costs mean both higher crude values and stronger refining economics.
